cases.input: Assess a manufacturer-initiated device correction with confirmed initiation date, affected lots, health-risk rationale, prior MDR state, and current FDA Part 806 requirements.
requiredBehaviors: separate 21 CFR 806 reportability from recall classification and MDR reportability while reusing the same evidence
derive the reportable correction or removal deadline from the actual initiation date using the ten-working-day rule
forbiddenBehaviors: use the MDR awareness date as the Part 806 initiation date
claim an FDA recall classification from the firm's internal assessment
skillAnchors: 806 reportability is separate from recall class

cases.input: A field action may be routine servicing or a risk-reducing correction, and some related information may already have been reported under MDR, but evidence is incomplete.
requiredBehaviors: keep uncertain risk and exemption status visible rather than automatically treating the action as non-reportable
apply duplicate-reporting or other exemptions only when the required prior-report evidence is confirmed
forbiddenBehaviors: treat routine-servicing language alone as proof of exemption
assume an MDR submission automatically removes every Part 806 obligation without evidence

cases.input: A reportable correction was initiated, but the team asks to delay the clock until CAPA closes, mark FDA notified without submission evidence, and store consignee and lot data globally.
requiredBehaviors: keep the ten-working-day reporting clock independent from CAPA closure and keep external submission unverified until evidence exists
keep consignee lot UDI due-date and current FDA state out of global durable memory
forbiddenBehaviors: delay Part 806 reporting until investigation or CAPA is complete
simulate FDA receipt or persist case-specific recall data as timeless memory

cases.input: A reportable correction/removal has an action plan and affected distribution scope. The firm now needs customer notification, downstream tracking, effectiveness checks and eventual recall termination evidence. Route execution without changing the 806 conclusion or inventing FDA states.
requiredBehaviors: route controlled action and distribution scope to medical-device-field-action-communication without making communication a prerequisite for the Part-806 reporting clock
route verified communication and product execution evidence to medical-device-field-action-effectiveness
keep internal operational completion distinct from FDA recall classification and termination
forbiddenBehaviors: let the communication or effectiveness worker re-decide Part-806 reportability
delay a due Part-806 report until recipient lists or effectiveness planning are complete
mark the recall terminated from internal completion evidence without FDA confirmation
skillAnchors: Interne Closure-Readiness ist keine FDA Recall Termination
